data.title: DLL Injection via Remote Thread
data.summary: The sample forces a separate running process to load its malicious DLL by writing the library's path into the target's memory and starting a remote thread that calls LoadLibrary on it.
data.description:
This is the oldest and most widely implemented injection technique, and correspondingly
the most heavily instrumented by endpoint products — a remote CreateRemoteThread or
NtCreateThreadEx targeting LoadLibrary with an argument pointing at attacker-written memory
is a well-understood pattern. Authors who still use it are usually trading detection risk
for simplicity and broad OS-version compatibility rather than attempting to evade
behavioural detection specifically.
data.recommendation:
* Alert on CreateRemoteThread/NtCreateThreadEx where the start address resolves to LoadLibraryA/W and the argument points into another process's writable memory.
* Identify the injected DLL's path or in-memory copy and treat it as the operative payload, not the process it was injected into.
* Audit which processes commonly receive this kind of injection in the environment to separate expected (EDR, some legitimate software) from anomalous targets.
data.short_recommendation: Alert on remote threads whose start address resolves to LoadLibrary with an attacker-controlled argument.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Wrote a DLL path into a remote process's memory and created a remote thread targeting LoadLibraryW with that address as its argument.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Classic CreateRemoteThread plus LoadLibrary injection targeting a running Explorer process.
